findings.passage: He has kept working, through _We Live in Time_, _After the Hunt_, _The Magic Faraway Tree_ and _The Uprising_, so what changed, by his account, is why he works.
findings.problem: The Three rebuttal is the part of the argument most exposed to an event already on the calendar. It rests on 2024 self-reports: "two thirds of my ambition died" (C19) and the Oscar "meant something to me in the past" (C30). Line 152 compresses that to "an Oscar once meant something to him." The frozen evidence for the same Chicken Shop Date exchange (S13, ~08:19–09:53) also has "when I didn't win a couple of times I was like I guess maybe I should give up on that dream" and, moments later, "my longing is back for it yeah but then I'm like trying to please you". Those lines are omitted, so the draft makes the achievement pull look more settled-in-the-past than the source does. The foreseeable test is Artificial: a Guadagnino prestige film with a December 25, 2026 US release, which puts him in the 2027 awards season. If he campaigns, is nominated or wins, "what changed ... is why he works" will read as written before the evidence came in. C19 and C30 are marked stable with no review_trigger, and C36's trigger covers film status, not the Three argument.
findings.acceptance_test: (1) Line 152 and the Chicken Shop Date paragraph reflect the full exchange, including the "give up on that dream" and "my longing is back for it" lines, with the same unlabeled-caption caveat and the flirt-format framing. If they are excluded, the draft says why. (2) The Three rebuttal is phrased as dated self-report ("In 2024 he told Cooper..."), not a settled present-tense conclusion. (3) C19 and C30 are reclassified time_sensitive or unresolved, with a review_trigger such as: "After the 2027 awards season (nominations and ceremony, early 2027) and Artificial's press tour: if Garfield campaigns for, is nominated for or publicly discusses an Oscar, re-test the Three section and the bio honors list." (4) A reader in 2031 would not find the Three section obviously overtaken by a 2027 awards run.

findings.passage: He describes a "Truman show feeling like, is this everything? It can't be everything," and says that while he was never a suicidal kid, "I was enraged at the concept of this being everything."
findings.problem: The draft calls this "the hinge of the type argument." It repeats "enraged" in the hook, in the meta description ("As a boy, Andrew Garfield was enraged that ordinary life might be everything") and in the Type 9 FAQ. The word doing the discriminating work is "enraged": anger, not settling. It exists only in a third-party podscripts.co auto-transcript (S06). The record's own open research task says "Verify against audio before any expansion", and the print relay (S07) supports only the gentler "I feel there is more." Over five years this is also the most fragile link in the chain. It is an aggregator transcript, and the Esquire and Vanity Fair corroboration is cited only through Yahoo syndications (S07, S28), which often expire. If those pages go, a reader cannot check the line the Four-versus-Nine argument turns on.
findings.acceptance_test: Option (a): confirm the "enraged" sentence against the WTF episode 1359 audio, record the timestamp in the S06 locator (~00:40:40–00:42:44), and link the official episode page next to the transcript. Option (b): reword the hook, description and Type 9 FAQ so the discriminator rests on print-corroborated wording ("I feel there is more ... if it doesn't exist, I am in big trouble"), and attribute "enraged" explicitly as transcript wording wherever it remains. Either way, thesis-bearing Esquire (C10, C11) and Vanity Fair (C44) quotes cite the original publisher URL or an archived snapshot in addition to the syndicated copy, recorded in the evidence locators.

findings.passage: Publicity explains when he talks about grief. It doesn't explain why he describes it in the same terms across nine years.
findings.problem: The grief sources in the record run from January 2017 (America, S01) to October 2024 (Cooper S05, Elmo S04), about seven to eight years. The only 2026 source (S12, the America podcast) covers longing, the mask and ordinariness, not grief, as far as it was read. "Nine years" seems to be counted to the latest event rather than to the latest grief evidence. A computed span like this also drifts as the article ages.
findings.acceptance_test: Replace the span with absolute years that match the cited grief sources (e.g., "from 2017 to 2024"), or add a 2025–2026 grief source to the evidence record and cite it. Update C38's passage to match.

findings.passage: In September 2026 he told a Jesuit podcast that he wants to "free myself into my ordinariness." The distance between those two sentences is the story of his personality.
findings.problem: The thesis passes the five-year test. Remove the September 2026 podcast and the arc still stands on the 2017 "hidden life", the April 2022 "just be ordinary for a while" and the 2022 "I wasn't special" story, which has three accounts (Maron, Vanity Fair, Cooper). The persona_title ("The Seeker Learning to Be Ordinary") echoes the same 2026 wording. If he says something different in 2027–2031, the opening will look dated even though the argument is not.
findings.acceptance_test: Run a deletion test: remove the September 2026 sentence from the hook, and the remaining pairing should still read as complete. One option is to make the two sentences "enraged at the concept of this being everything" and the already-quoted "I understood that I wasn't special". The 2026 quote then stays as the dated latest instance where it already appears in the "I wasn't special" section. If the 2026 line stays in the hook, frame it explicitly as the most recent point in the pattern, and give C43/C49 a review_trigger for new long-form self-accounts.

assessment: Five-year test: the thesis passes. The core evidence is dated and spread across 2017–2024: the pre-bereavement America interview, Colbert in 2021, the 2022 ocean story with three accounts, and Cooper in 2024. Removing both the September 2026 podcast and the October 2026 film status leaves the Four argument and the Nine discriminator intact. The ending relies on nothing recent, and the profile wisely avoids relationship status. Weak points: one status sentence that goes stale within a day (future-01). The Three rebuttal is the section most exposed to a foreseeable event, Artificial's 2027 awards season, and trims the Oscar exchange (future-02). The hinge quote depends on a single auto-transcript hosted by an aggregator (future-03). There is also a computed year span, a hook endpoint pinned to a three-week-old podcast, a changelog reference in reader copy, and a 59-claim record where only C36 has a review_trigger. Similarity: the tripped Kacey Musgraves pair is the stock Type 4 definition ("something essential is missing") and the Bryan Johnson pair is "organized around". Both are ordinary type vocabulary; the actual argument here is distinct, so this is not a finding. Publish-time note for DJ, not the editor: frontmatter date and lastmod are 2026-06-09, earlier than the September 2026 sources cited. The runner preserves these and lastmod is DJ-managed, so it should be reconciled at publish, not in this pass.
